correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge5\), the minimum-state characterization follows from the exact closed-neighborhood traces and two-per-side necessity/sufficiency. Legal moves must slide into the unique vacant matched index with a side-count >=3, yielding exact degree and edge sum. \(n=5\) has only p=q=2 and is frozen. \(n=6\) has invariant three-subset S and twenty K3,3 components. For every \(n\ge7\), explicit three-slide sequences recolor any chosen index at a fixed hole and explicit two-slide sequences move the hole with p,q>=3, so the full graph is connected. The proof checks edge adjacency and population boundaries. Independent exhaustive programs construct original graph codes through n=9 and ternary state graphs through n=12; all counts and components agree, but these finite checks are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete mobility classification across an infinite natural family of optimal neighborhood-identification configurations. The \(n=5\) frozen, \(n=6\) K3,3 fragmentation, and sharp \(n\ge7\) connectivity phase transition show a substantive boundary between sensor relocation by local slides and static optimum-code enumeration. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or known table recomputation: the all-n theorem needs explicit nontrivial legal recoloring and hole-transfer lemmas. The exact edge count quantifies mobility but is not offered as the sole contribution.
